[EVALUATION RESULT]
Question: Let \(\|x\|\) denote the distance from a real number \(x\) to the nearest integer. Fix integers \(d\ge 2\) and \(k\ge 1\). Which of the following is the strongest statement asserting the existence of a constant, depending only on \(d\), \(k\), and any indicated \(\varepsilon>0\), that works uniformly for all \(N\ge 2\) and all \(\beta\in\mathbb R\)?
Predicted label: 'D'
Predicted text: 'For every \\(\\varepsilon>0\\), there exists a constant \\(C_{d,k,\\varepsilon}>0\\), depending only on \\(d\\), \\(k\\), and \\(\\varepsilon\\), such that for every \\(N\\ge 2\\) and every \\(\\beta\\in\\mathbb R\\), there exist integers \\(b_1,\\dots,b_k\\) with \\(1\\le b_1,\\dots,b_k\\le N\\) and\n\\[\n\\left\\|\\sum_{j=1}^k b_j^{1/d}-\\beta\\right\\|\\le C_{d,k,\\varepsilon}N^{-k/d+\\varepsilon}.\n\\]'
Correct label: 'D'
Correct text: 'For every \\(\\varepsilon>0\\), there exists a constant \\(C_{d,k,\\varepsilon}>0\\), depending only on \\(d\\), \\(k\\), and \\(\\varepsilon\\), such that for every \\(N\\ge 2\\) and every \\(\\beta\\in\\mathbb R\\), there exist integers \\(b_1,\\dots,b_k\\) with \\(1\\le b_1,\\dots,b_k\\le N\\) and\n\\[\n\\left\\|\\sum_{j=1}^k b_j^{1/d}-\\beta\\right\\|\\le C_{d,k,\\varepsilon}N^{-k/d+\\varepsilon}.\n\\]'
Exact Match: 1.0
